## About

The **GEP Simulator** turns satellite and LiDAR layers into an interactive **Gross Ecosystem
Product (GEP)** index for ecosystem services. Its guiding idea is *structural quality instead
of area maximisation*: structure- and condition indicators are weighted, so a species-rich,
well-connected patch scores higher than an equally large but structurally poor one — and a
naïve reduction of nature to a single tradable monetary value is deliberately avoided.

Each supply-side ecosystem service (cooling from land-surface temperature, carbon and biomass
from NDVI, stormwater retention from sealing, plus air-quality, noise mitigation, landscape
aesthetics and production services) is combined with a **Vertical Structure Index (VSI)**
derived from LiDAR (canopy height, rugosity, cover, foliage-height diversity). An interactive
slider sets how strongly structure boosts or penalises the score:

```
GEP = clamp( Σ (weightᵢ · ESSᵢ) · (1 + w·(VSI − 0.5)·2),  0, 1 )
```

Built as the **P1 (supply-side)** application demo for the **GEP@HHN** project (Hochschule
Heilbronn); spatial context (rarity, connectivity, demand → P2) and monetisation (P3) are
intentionally not yet folded in. The demo region is **Utrecht / Wilhelminapark (NL)**, where
open AHN LiDAR point clouds are freely available; Sentinel-2, Landsat and WorldCover round out
the free, globally reproducible data basis.
